stance_basis: Staff critiques applicant's analysis of coldwater habitat loss and projects elimination of trout habitat under combined project operation
summary: FPC Staff challenges the applicant's characterization of habitat loss in Jocassee Reservoir, arguing that a simple year-to-year comparison understates the cumulative thermal impacts of the Jocassee pumped storage plant operating in conjunction with Lake Keowee. Staff further projects that under full combined operation of the Jocassee and Bad Creek Projects, optimum coldwater trout habitat in the main body of Jocassee Reservoir would be eliminated. Staff's position implies that the project as proposed raises serious unresolved concerns about aquatic habitat impacts.
complaint_summary: Staff concludes that under the proposed plan of operation for both the Jocassee and Bad Creek Projects, optimum coldwater trout habitat in the main body of Jocassee Reservoir would be eliminated.

statement.text: Whether or not the trout habitat in the main body of Jocassee Reservoir would be eliminated under the combined operation of the Jocassee and Bad Creek Projects would depend on the operating plant factors of the projects and the amounts of cooler water they remove from the reservoir. Under the proposed plan of operation for both projects, however, it is expected that the optimum habitat (20°C; 5 mg/1 DO) would be eliminated in the main body of the reservoir.

statement.closing_anchor: it is expected that the optimum habitat (20°C; 5 mg/1 DO) would be eliminated in the main body of the reservoir.

summary_quote: Staff believes that comparing the depth and thickness of habitat loss in Jocassee Reservoir for 1974 and 1975 does not fully explain the effect the operation of the Jocassee pumped storage plant, in conjunction with Lake Keowee, has on the reservoir habitat.
